item: Doing nothing is always an option
how_handled: It is priced at $0 and every offer has to beat it.
Chance of churn x chance the action saves them x value of the account, minus the offer cost and a contact cost.
About $76.46 a month margin over 24 months, weighted for the chance they leave anyway (0.99% a month) and discounted 10% a year.
The next version picks at a 10% save rate, scaling each action's rate down to match.
A fix-first callback costs $15, a check-in $2, plus an annoyance cost of $2 to $6 per contact.

item: Exemption: a new phone the customer chose
how_handled: A bill rise that is only a new phone payment doesn't block (850 accounts); new phone plus a promo ending still blocks (71).

item: We don't use 'bill went up' alone
how_handled: That would flag 4,679 accounts, mostly cents of noise.
With an open support issue in the last 90 days, the only message allowed is a fix; 25 perk reminders became fix callbacks.
No payoff or upgrade-timing message; contacting them early is pure timing and loses money (-$156). 12 of them still get an unrelated fix call for an open issue.
No trade-in messages: at a $0 device margin the nudge never adds money at any take rate. Trade-in value shows only as a bill/app line.

item: Cheaper plans are never a message
how_handled: They go on the bill as tap-to-confirm; unprompted plan recommendations raised churn from about 6% to 10% in a field test.

item: No upsell after a bill shock
how_handled: Plan step-ups and phone upgrades are blocked for 90 days after a promo ends or the bill jumps 15% or more.
An upsell is blocked if it raises the bill by more than 25% (40% when a line is already over its data cap); never based on income.
At most one proactive contact per account per quarter; the sandbox has no outreach log, so this is a hook, and each run sends at most one message.
Opted-out accounts get no marketing; the sandbox has no opt-out field, so this is a hook.
Every text ends with 'Reply STOP to opt out'; in-app, email and calls each carry their own opt-out. The run fails if one is missing.
Only 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time (a send-time rule; the sandbox has no time zone).
Each goes by the customer's own stated preference, not a ranking: 74 in-app, 64 texts, 32 emails, 14 calls.
Over the 5,000 regular accounts: 5,000 scored, 500 flagged, 182 messaged, 64 by text (2 messages go to demo accounts).
Texts start 'T-Mobile:' and say Reply YES/STOP; in-app says 'Tap to...'; email says 'Use the link below...'; calls are a short script.
18 messages are in Spanish (usted); 166 in English, and every row also carries a Spanish version.
Texts at most 320 characters (longest 257 English, 293 Spanish); other channels at most 420.
